Tom/So — I populated the attached concessions_model.xlsx with a conservative AtlasPay profile based on the numbers you shared in the demo (avg tokens/day, pilot cohort size, expected Q3 ramp). Highlights:

- One-time buyout ($250k) vs graduated credits (60% / 40% / 20% / 10% over 4 quarters): the buyout gives immediate cash relief but pushes unit cost higher in months 4–12 if usage ramps above the assumed baseline.
- Graduated credits tied to committed quarterly usage preserve better alignment; AtlasPay sees lower effective unit cost during the ramp and Redwood retains better visibility into long-term revenue.
- Break-even sensitivity: with your expected ramp, credits model is ~8–10% cheaper for AtlasPay over 12 months vs a flat $250k buyout when factoring in onboarding and runbook hours.

I also attached a short competitor comparison (orbital-comparison.pdf) that notes Orbital’s higher latency at 95th pct and limited KV cache support (they price separately for inference cache). That drives operational cost on your side.

[attachment: concessions_model.xlsx]
[attachment: orbital-comparison.pdf]

I’ll flag two negotiation levers that close quickly: 1) a 3-month pilot credit that covers the pilot cohort tokens (no long-term license commitment), and 2) a time-limited onboarding services credit if AtlasPay commits to a 9–12 month reserved capacity minimum.

-Ben

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is exactly what procurement needs. A couple of follow-ups:
1) If we go with graduated credits linked to committed usage, how do you handle overrun months? Are overruns billed at list or do you apply a blended rate?
2) The Orbital buyout is effectively a credit they apply up-front, but it requires a 12-month minimum committed spend at a 15% discount. If we do a credits model with a 9–12 month reserved commitment, is there a simplified MOU we can review that lists the credit schedule?

Also — can you model a hybrid: $100k upfront credit + smaller graduated credits (40/30/20/10) with a 9-month reserved term? That would align with our CFO’s preference for some immediate relief.

Tom

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@atlaspay.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Concessions framework + draft MOU

Forwarding a draft MOU and a suggested hybrid concessions structure. I recommend the hybrid below as negotiable language — it preserves Redwood’s revenue visibility while giving AtlasPay immediate runway:

- Upfront credit: $100,000 applied to first invoice (non-refundable)
- Graduated usage credits: applied as % offsets against monthly token charges on committed reserved capacity: 40% Q1, 30% Q2, 20% Q3, 10% Q4 (applies only up to committed baseline; overruns billed at blended rate = list price less 10%)
- Commitment: 9-month reserved capacity (minimum commit equal to 70% of expected ramp month tokens)
- Pilot coverage: 30-day pilot credit covering pilot cohort tokens (no commit required)

Attached: mou-draft.pdf with the credit schedule language and a simple termination clause tied to notice periods and unused credit reconciliation.

[attachment: mou-draft.pdf]

If this looks good we can produce a redline and a short one-page summary that procurement can send to the CFO.

-Marissa Cole
